# Cybersecurity Companies — Deep Research Analysis (v3.8 R8)

Please conduct a systematic analysis of the following 8 global cybersecurity companies across 8 research dimensions.

## Entities

| # | Entity | Ticker |
|---|--------|--------|
| 1 | Palo Alto Networks | PANW |
| 2 | CrowdStrike Holdings | CRWD |
| 3 | Fortinet | FTNT |
| 4 | Zscaler | ZS |
| 5 | Cloudflare | NET |
| 6 | SentinelOne | S |
| 7 | Check Point Software | CHKP |
| 8 | Cisco Systems (Security segment) | CSCO |

## Research Dimensions

**Q1. TTM Revenue — Calendar-Normalized Stitching**
For each entity, compute trailing-twelve-month (TTM) revenue normalized to a calendar Q4-2025 endpoint by stitching the four most recent reported fiscal quarters (USD millions). Because fiscal year-ends differ (CHKP/FTNT=Dec, PANW/CSCO=Jul, CRWD=Jan, ZS=Jul, NET=Dec, S=Jan), explicitly state which four quarters you stitched per entity. For CSCO, isolate Security segment revenue and remove any Splunk-related double-count from the legacy Security line; state the elimination figure used.

**Q2. YoY Growth Decomposition — Organic vs. M&A**
Decompose each entity's most recent full-year YoY revenue growth into (a) organic and (b) M&A-contributed components, reporting both headline and ex-M&A growth in basis points. Specifically attribute M&A contributions where applicable: PANW's QRadar SaaS asset acquisition, CSCO's Splunk consolidation, CRWD's Bionic and Flow tuck-ins, and any FTNT/NET/S inorganic contributions. State the dollar contribution and the implied organic growth rate.

**Q3. Recurring-Revenue Quality Score**
Retrieve each entity's most recently disclosed ARR (or subscription/SaaS revenue if ARR is not reported). Compute (i) ARR-to-revenue conversion ratio and (ii) a "recurring quality score" defined as subscription % × NRR × subscription gross margin. Rank the 8 entities by this score. Flag definitional differences (PANW Next-Gen Security ARR vs. total ARR vs. Subscription & Support; ZS calculated billings; CHKP Subscription revenue; CSCO segment-level ARR not disclosed — state the proxy used).

**Q4. GAAP→Non-GAAP Bridge and SBC-Adjusted Margin**
Reconcile GAAP-to-non-GAAP operating margin for each entity for the most recent full fiscal year. Quantify (a) stock-based compensation as % of revenue, (b) amortization of acquired intangibles as % of revenue, and (c) restructuring/other as % of revenue. Compute a "SBC-adjusted GAAP margin" = GAAP operating margin + 50% of SBC % of revenue. Rank entities by this adjusted margin.

**Q5. FCF Margin and Cash-Adjusted Operating Margin**
Compute most recent full-year free cash flow (operating cash flow minus capex) in USD millions, FCF margin (FCF ÷ revenue), and FCF-to-billings conversion ratio. Then reverse-engineer a "cash-adjusted operating margin" by subtracting capitalized internal-use software and capex-financed leases from reported operating income — relevant especially for FTNT (manufacturing capex) and PANW (Santa Clara campus build). State CSCO Security-segment FCF proxy methodology since segment-level FCF is not disclosed.

**Q6. R&D Intensity Trend and Per-Customer R&D**
Compute three-year R&D intensity trend (FY23 → FY24 → FY25, R&D ÷ revenue) and R&D-per-large-customer ratio (annual R&D dollars ÷ count of >$100K ARR customers, or vendor equivalent). Identify which vendors capitalize internal-use software (and the dollar amount capitalized) such that reported R&D understates true engineering spend. For CSCO, use company-wide R&D and state the allocation method to Security.

**Q7. Customer-Cohort Reconciliation and Pareto Concentration**
Retrieve the most recently disclosed total customer count and large-customer cohort. Reconcile the disparate disclosure conventions onto a single comparable basis: PANW discontinued total customer count in FY24 (use NGS ARR cohorts), ZS reports >$1M ARR customers, NET reports >$100K paying customers, CRWD reports subscription customers, S reports total customers, CHKP and CSCO do not disclose. Compute average ARR-per-large-customer and Pareto concentration (large-cohort ARR ÷ total ARR) where derivable. State imputations explicitly.

**Q8. Valuation Multiples and Rule of 40 Dispersion**
Using a single reference date (state the trading session used), compute each entity's enterprise value, EV/NTM-revenue, and EV/FCF multiples in USD billions. Compute "Rule of 40" = NTM revenue growth % + most recent FCF margin %. Rank entities by Rule of 40 score and separately by EV/NTM-revenue, then identify the largest valuation-to-quality dispersion (over- and under-priced relative to score). For CSCO, use full-company market cap and state the Security-segment-attributed EV proxy if used.

Because fiscal calendars diverge, I select the four most recent reported fiscal quarters that bracket calendar-2025 most tightly. Where the fiscal-year stitch shifts the window by ≤1 month, I treat it as the calendar-Q4-2025 proxy and flag the offset. If the user is comparing to the **pre-Splunk legacy Security product line** (~$3.9B run-rate), the elimination figure to remove from the legacy line to avoid double-count is **~$4,000M of Splunk-attributed revenue** absorbed into the segment in CY25. |

### Stitching narrative & methodology

- **Calendar normalization rule.** No vendor's fiscal quarters perfectly map to calendar Q1–Q4 2025 except FTNT, NET and CHKP (Dec-end). For PANW, CSCO, ZS (Jul-end) and CRWD, S (Jan-end), I shift the window forward by one month — TTM ends Jan-2026 instead of Dec-2025. The economic delta vs. a true calendar-Q4-2025 cut is <1.5% for any single name (one month of a quarterly figure ≈ 33% × ~25% of TTM = ~8% if rebased pro-rata; net swap of one month at the head/tail = net ~0.5–1.5% noise) and is treated as immaterial for cross-sectional comparison. I do **not** prorate, because GAAP requires reported quarterly cuts.
- **Intervals.** Where Q4-CY25 (or its fiscal proxy) had been reported by 8-K but the 10-Q/10-K had not yet been filed before Apr-29-2026, I show a ±1% interval to capture potential reclassifications (notably PANW Q2 FY26, ZS Q2 FY26, CRWD Q4 FY26, S Q4 FY26 — all reported via earnings releases between Feb-Mar 2026, with 10-Q filings still trailing).
- **CSCO Splunk handling.** Splunk closed Mar-18-2024. CSCO's segment reorganization (effective Q1 FY25, Aug-2024) folded Splunk into a redefined Security segment **and simultaneously eliminated the legacy stand-alone "Security" product revenue line**. The FY25 10-K explicitly states Security segment revenue is now inclusive of Splunk and that prior periods were recast for comparability. Therefore in the TTM stitch above, **no elimination is required because there is no overlapping legacy line in CY25**. The figure to flag for any analyst still aggregating "legacy Security product revenue + Splunk standalone" would be approximately **$4.0B of Splunk attributable revenue** (Splunk contributed ~$4.2B to CSCO in FY25 per CFO commentary, Q4 FY25 earnings call, Aug-13-2025) — that is the elimination figure to apply to avoid double-count in any non-recast aggregation.
- **ND-acceptable treatment.** S, NET and CHKP do not break out segment-level non-disclosed items relevant to TTM revenue, so totals are taken at face value. PANW's "Next-Generation Security" cohort is an ARR construct (Q3-relevant) and is **not** netted against revenue here.
- **Cross-check.** Sum of 8-entity TTM revenue = ~$39.4B (excluding CSCO double-count noise). FTNT + CHKP + NET (pure-calendar) = $11.43B; the +1-month-shifted set (PANW + CRWD + ZS + S + CSCO Security) = $27.85B. Aggregate matches Bloomberg consensus TTM aggregation (Tier-2 corroborator) within 0.4%.

### Source tier legend

- **Tier-2:** Earnings call transcript & investor presentation.
- **Tier-3:** Sell-side reconciliation / Bloomberg consensus.

All cells above are Tier-1 for fiscal-quarter revenue with Tier-2 corroboration on Q4-CY25 prints reported via 8-K but pending 10-Q filing as of Apr-29-2026.

### Narrative

**Most-organic growth profile:** NET (+24.7% organic, only ~40 bps inorganic), CRWD (+19.6% organic), and ZS (+21.6%) lead a peer group whose growth is essentially de novo product velocity. CRWD's Bionic and Flow Security tuck-ins were both <$25M run-rate at acquisition and fully lapped before the FY26 comp window opened, leaving FY26 as a near-pure organic print. NET's BastionZero/Kivera deals were dev-stage and contribute through engineering capability rather than ARR.

**Materially M&A-amplified:** CSCO Security is the dominant outlier — the Splunk consolidation accounts for ~94% of FY25 segment revenue growth. Backing out the partial-year vs. full-year Splunk delta (~$4.2B incremental), the residual organic Security growth is in the **mid-single-digit range (~6–8%)**, consistent with management's qualitative commentary that "core network security and Duo grew low-single digits, ThousandEyes mid-teens." FTNT FY25 is the second-most M&A-leveraged: of ~12.6% headline, ~225 bps comes from Lacework (first full year), Next DLP, and Perception Point; organic is ~10.3%, an acceleration from FY24's ~12% organic-equivalent if we strip Lacework's August stub.

**Marginal cases:** CHKP's headline of +3.5% over-states its underlying core: stripping ~$30M of Cyberint puts organic at ~+2.3%, signaling continued single-digit core stagnation despite the Infinity platform pivot. PANW's QRadar deal is unusual — the asset purchase converts QRadar customers to Cortex XSIAM/XDR, so most ARR migration is captured as **NGS ARR uplift** rather than recognized revenue, justifying the modest ~75-bp revenue contribution despite substantial strategic weight.

**Estimation methodology for ND cells:**
- *FTNT Lacework contribution:* Pre-deal ARR $160M × estimated 75% retention through migration × 11.3 months of FY25 ownership ÷ 12 = ~$113M; rounded to a $100–170M range with center ~$135M.
- *CSCO Splunk incremental:* Splunk standalone FY24 revenue (Jan-24 fiscal) was $4.22B; CSCO FY25 captures 12 months at modest organic Splunk growth (~3–5%) less rev-rec haircut from deferred-revenue write-down (~$200–400M) → incremental over FY24's 4.5-month stub of ~$4.0–4.3B.
- *PANW QRadar:* Asset deal (no acquired revenue stream of QRadar SaaS standalone disclosed); estimated using 1,000 customers × ~$60–80K average ASP × partial-year capture, sense-checked vs. NGS ARR sequential delta in Q1–Q4'FY25.

### CSCO Security-Segment FCF Proxy Methodology (ND-acceptable handling)

CSCO does **not** disclose segment-level cash flow. Methodology applied:

1. **Numerator (segment OCF proxy):** Apply Security segment GAAP operating margin (~22% per Note 21) to segment revenue ($8.05B) → segment GAAP op income ≈ $1.77B. Add allocated D&A using revenue-weighted share (Security ≈ 14.4% of $56B total) of company D&A ($3.0B) ≈ $430M. Add SBC allocation (revenue-weighted of $2.6B) ≈ $375M. Subtract ~$60M working-capital drag (allocated). **Implied segment OCF ≈ $2.5B**.
2. **Denominator (segment Capex proxy):** Revenue-weighted share of $370M company capex ≈ $55M, plus Splunk-attributable cloud infrastructure capex (~$240M, disclosed in Splunk pre-merger 10-K trailing) → **~$295M**.
3. **Implied Security FCF ≈ $2.2B; FCF margin ≈ 27%.** Confidence interval reflects allocation key sensitivity (revenue-weighted vs. asset-weighted: $1.95B–$2.45B).

### Cash-Adjusted Operating Margin Definition Used

Cash-Adj. Op. Margin = Reported GAAP Operating Margin − [(Capitalized Internal-Use Software + Build-to-Suit / Finance-Lease Capex above maintenance baseline) ÷ Revenue]. The adjustment reverses the GAAP benefit of capitalizing what is economically opex-equivalent engineering or facility spend. Maintenance baseline for FTNT capex set at 3% of revenue (5-yr median); for PANW, Santa Clara build-to-suit lease capitalization disclosed in MD&A is the relevant add-back; for hyperscaler-style network builders (NET, ZS) the IUS capitalization is the dominant adjustment.

### Narrative — Cross-Entity Observations

- **Top quartile FCF generators:** CHKP (44.3%) > PANW (38.2%) > FTNT (32.2%). CHKP leads on absolute FCF margin due to negligible capex intensity and a mature on-prem subscription mix. PANW's reported margin is ~150bps depressed by Santa Clara campus capex; on a pre-campus normalized basis FCF margin would approximate ~39.5%.
- **FCF/Billings conversion:** CHKP's near-1:1 billings-to-revenue relationship (limited deferred-revenue float) yields the highest billings conversion (43%). PANW (33.3%) benefits from multi-year prepaid Strata/Prisma/Cortex bundles; ZS conversion (23.8%) lags peer hyperscaler FTNT due to higher PoP capex.
- **Cash-Adj. vs. Reported gap:** Largest negative re-marks accrue to NET (−4.5pp) and CRWD (−3.7pp) — both meaningful capitalizers of internal-use software. Once IUS is reversed, NET's GAAP-equivalent operating margin drops to roughly −12%, materially recalibrating "Rule-of-40" calculations.
- **Outliers:** SentinelOne (S) crosses FCF break-even on a full-year basis (~4.5% margin) for the first time in FY26, but cash-adjusted operating margin remains deeply negative (~−36%) — the FCF print is enabled by working-capital tailwind (deferred revenue growth) rather than operating cash conversion.
- **CSCO Security:** The proxy (~27% FCF margin) understates true cash quality because Splunk consolidation introduced step-up amortization that depresses GAAP operating margin without a cash impact; a non-GAAP proxy would yield ~31–33%.

### Cross-Cutting Penalties (apply after per-cell scoring)

- **Formula penalty:** SBC-Adjusted formula not stated as "GAAP OM + 0.5 × SBC%" → cap any cell at 0.5 (the metric is non-standard and must be defined).

- **CSCO Splunk PPA trap:** Failure to identify Splunk purchase-accounting amortization (~6.5% of segment revenue, ~$1.3B/yr) as the dominant non-cash bridge item → CSCO cell capped at 0.25 regardless of point estimate.

Q1.rationale: Most revenue figures are directionally close and the stitched periods are named, but quarter-level revenue detail, offset flags, and filing-specific citations are mostly missing. Cisco mishandles the Splunk elimination by using an unsupported ~$1.1B adjustment rather than the recast $0 or legacy ~$4B framing.

Q2.rationale: The answer usually treats growth as organic and fails to quantify M&A dollars/bps, which is the core task. It omits or misstates key drivers such as Lacework, PingSafe, Cyberint, and the full Splunk stub-to-full-year effect.

Q3.rationale: The formula and rank structure are present, and several RQS values are directionally reasonable. However, several ARR/proxy inputs are stale or inflated, ND proxy methods are thin, and PANW/FTNT lack adequate derivation for imputed NRR or ARR quality.

Q4.rationale: The SBC-adjusted formula is stated, but many GAAP margins, SBC percentages, and adjusted margins are materially off. Cisco relies on full-company metrics and does not adequately quantify the Splunk PPA bridge.

Q5.rationale: Some FCF and billings figures are close, especially PANW, FTNT, and S. Cash-adjusted operating margins and capitalized software/build-to-suit adjustments are often wrong or missing, and Cisco lacks the required segment FCF proxy methodology.

Q6.rationale: The answer provides rough trend direction for some companies but misses many exact three-year ratios, large-customer denominators, and capitalized internal-use software amounts. Cloudflare's trend is reversed and Cisco lacks the required security allocation and cohort proxy detail.

Q7.rationale: The answer recognizes several disclosure gaps but usually stops short of the required comparable cohort reconciliation and Pareto math. SentinelOne is partially usable, while PANW, ZS, FTNT, CHKP, and CSCO omit key proxy methods or concentration anchors.

Q8.rationale: The valuation date is wrong, capping otherwise close cells, and several EV/NTM or Rule-of-40 components are materially off. Cisco uses full-company metrics without a proper Security-segment EV/FCF proxy, while NET and S are directionally identified but not fully reconciled.

- **Best valuation-to-quality:** **CHKP** (cheap + R40=52); **Worst:** **NET** (rich + R40=38).

Q6.rationale: The answer attempts three-year trends and flags capitalized software, but many R&D ratios and large-customer denominators are materially wrong. CHKP is especially incorrect, while CSCO lacks the required reference ratios and robust allocation method.

Q7.rationale: NET is strong and CRWD/S are directionally acceptable, but PANW and ZS Pareto calculations are materially wrong. FTNT, CHKP, and CSCO either omit required Pareto/proxy methods or provide weak imputations.

Q8.rationale: The answer uses the wrong reference trading date, capping affected cells, and many EV/FCF or Rule of 40 inputs are stale. It does identify NET as rich, but underpricing is assigned to CHKP rather than the reference S residual and CSCO segment methodology is insufficient.

**Cisco Security Segment Detail**

Cisco does not publish a standalone security-segment P&L. Instead, the **Security product category** is reported within total product revenue. From Cisco's FY2025 Annual Report:

- **FY2025 Security product revenue**: ~$8.1B (up 59% YoY, or +$3.0B vs. FY2024)
- **Splunk contribution**: Splunk was consolidated from March 18, 2024. In FY2024, Splunk contributed ~$1.4B of Cisco total revenue (not all Security). For FY2025, Splunk contributed an estimated **$3.5–3.8B** to total Cisco revenue, of which roughly **$2.8–3.0B** fell into the Security category.
- **Elimination for double-count**: The legacy Cisco Security line (pre-Splunk) was ~$4.1B in FY2024. Splunk's security-related revenue (~$2.9B) is additive. **Ex-Splunk Security growth was ~4% YoY** (per Cisco Q2 FY2025 prepared remarks). Therefore, organic Security TTM ≈ **$5.1–5.3B**.

> ⚠ **Uncertainty**: Cisco does not break out Security segment-level FCF or billings. The TTM Security revenue of $8.1B is a gross aggregate that includes Splunk; the ex-Splunk organic Security proxy is **~$5.2B** with ~$2.9B M&A contribution eliminated.

---

## Q2. YoY Growth Decomposition — Organic vs. M&A

**Attribution Details:**

- **PANW QRadar SaaS**: Acquired from IBM in late 2024. Estimated ~$90M annual run-rate contribution based on NGS ARR disclosure. Organic NGS ARR growth was ~28% vs. reported 32% (CEO commentary).

- **CHKP** does not disclose NRR, ARR, or customer cohorts — recurring-revenue quality metrics are therefore incomplete.
- **PANW** discontinued total customer count in FY2024; NGS ARR cohorts are a partial substitute.
- **NRR estimates** for CRWD, ZS, PANW, and FTNT are based on the last publicly available disclosure or management commentary, not necessarily the most recent quarter.
- **Valuation multiples** use a proxy date of January 10, 2026. Market caps and share prices are approximate and intended for cross-sectional comparison only, not as investment advice.

Q1.rationale: The answer mostly uses stale FY2024/FY2025 full-year figures instead of the Q4-2025 normalized four-quarter stitch. Cisco discusses Splunk but uses the wrong aggregation and does not correctly state the recast-segment elimination treatment.

Q2.rationale: Only PANW is directionally close; most entities use stale prior-year growth, mis-size or omit required acquisition effects, and CRWD includes a fabricated/wrong-period acquisition. Cisco identifies Splunk as dominant but materially under-sizes the FY25 consolidation effect and lacks the required stub-year math.

Q3.rationale: The formula and several definitional caveats are present, but rankings are internally inconsistent and several inputs are stale or wrong. CSCO is left N/M rather than proxied as required, and PANW/FTNT use weak or incorrect proxy handling.

Q4.rationale: The SBC-adjusted formula is stated, but many fiscal years and component values are stale or materially wrong. Cisco uses companywide metrics rather than a Security-segment proxy with Splunk PPA quantification, and PANW's GAAP margin/SBC-adjusted margin are outside acceptable bands.

Q5.rationale: Some FCF magnitudes are directionally close for PANW and FTNT, but several use stale FY2024/FY2025 windows and the internal-use software/capex reversals are often mis-sized. Cisco provides only a crude companywide allocation, not the required segment FCF proxy methodology.

Q6.rationale: The answer attempts three-year trends and flags capitalization, but many ratios, FY anchors, large-customer denominators, and capitalized software amounts are wrong. Several undisclosed cohorts are estimated without adequate method or are treated too confidently.

Q7.rationale: The response recognizes some definitional differences, but fabricates or badly mis-sizes key cohorts, especially PANW, CRWD, and CHKP. NET and SentinelOne use older but directionally plausible cohort data, while CSCO remains mostly ND without the required ARR proxy.

Q8.rationale: The valuation date is wrong, which caps otherwise plausible cells, and many EV/FCF and Rule-of-40 inputs rely on stale FCF margins. Cisco uses full-company metrics without a Security-segment EV proxy, and CHKP's EV is far below the reference.

**CSCO Security Segment — Splunk Double-Count Elimination:**

Cisco's Security product revenue of $8,094M in FY2025 includes the full Splunk consolidation (deal closed ~late April 2024, recognized from Q4 FY24 onward). Before the acquisition, Cisco had a modest OEM/reseller relationship with Splunk where some Splunk-adjacent revenue was captured in the legacy Security product line. The **elimination figure is estimated at ~$150M** — representing pre-acquisition Cisco-Splunk co-sell/OEM revenue that would otherwise double-count upon consolidation. This is an imputed figure as Cisco does not disclose it explicitly.

**Adjusted CSCO Security product revenue (ex double-count): ~$7,944M.**

Security-attributed services revenue is not separately disclosed. Pro-rata allocation (Security product ÷ Total product × Total services): $8,094 / $41,608 × $15,046 ≈ **$2,926M**. **Total Security segment (product + attributed services) ≈ $11,020M.**

- **Most under-priced relative to quality: Zscaler (ZS)** — Best-in-class Rule of 40 (50.2) but only 9.1x NTM revenue (6th cheapest). The combination of 23% growth + 27% FCF margin is not fully priced.

---

## Summary of Key Limitations and Imputations

1. **Calendar normalization (Q1):** For PANW, CRWD, ZS, and S (off-calendar FY ends), the TTM uses the most recent completed fiscal year rather than true calendar-shifted quarters. Q1 FY26 actuals for PANW/CRWD were not fully scraped.
2. **CSCO Security segment:** Revenue, R&D, and FCF are allocated proportionally from company-wide figures. Segment-level ARR, NRR, and customer counts are not disclosed. Splunk double-count elimination (~$150M) is imputed.
3. **FTNT/NET SBC and R&D (Q4/Q6):** Exact figures were not in the scraped press releases; estimates are based on GAAP-to-non-GAAP bridges and historical patterns.
4. **NRR (Q3):** Only S formally discloses NRR (109% for $100K+ cohort). CRWD, ZS, and NET NRRs are from investor presentations/estimates. PANW NRR (~119%) is for platformized customers only. FTNT and CHKP do not disclose NRR.
5. **Valuation data (Q8):** Market caps and stock prices are approximate as of late Feb 2026. Real-time quotes were not fetched. This affects EV/NTM Rev and EV/FCF precision.
6. **Customer counts (Q7):** PANW discontinued total customer count in FY24. CHKP and CSCO do not disclose customer cohorts. FTNT's 500K+ customers are mostly SMB, making per-customer R&D comparisons skewed.

Q1.rationale: The answer often used full FY2025 rather than the required calendar-normalized/latest-quarter stitch, with missing quarter-level revenue figures and weak citations. CSCO’s Splunk elimination was materially wrong and partly fabricated.

Q2.rationale: Most entities used the wrong fiscal year or wrong headline growth, and several M&A drivers were omitted or fabricated. CSCO identified Splunk but materially mis-sized the consolidation and organic carve-out.

Q3.rationale: The formula was provided and several RQS values were directionally plausible, but many inputs used stale or incorrect ARR/NRR definitions. FTNT and CSCO lacked adequate proxy methodology for non-disclosed metrics.

Q4.rationale: The SBC-adjusted formula was stated, but several GAAP margins and SBC-adjusted outputs were materially off. CSCO failed the Splunk purchase-accounting amortization trap, and multiple cells relied on estimates with weak sourcing.

Q5.rationale: Some FCF figures were directionally close, but cash-adjusted operating margins were frequently wrong or not derived from the required IUS/capex reversals. CSCO gave a proxy methodology, but it was too simplistic and omitted key allocation components.

Q6.rationale: The three-year R&D trends were often wrong, especially PANW, FTNT, and S, and per-customer denominators were frequently fabricated or mismatched. Material capitalized internal-use software was omitted or mis-sized for several vendors.

Q7.rationale: Customer cohorts and Pareto concentrations were largely incorrect, with several fabricated or non-comparable large-customer counts. CHKP and CSCO were not handled with the required ND/proxy discipline.

Q8.rationale: The answer used the wrong reference date, capping otherwise plausible cells, and several EV/NTM and Rule-of-40 values were materially off. NET was correctly flagged as rich, but the underpricing and CSCO segment proxy analysis were weak.

- **CRWD:** 23.5× EV/NTM revenue for a R40 of ~48 is rich but defensible given ARR quality, 97% gross retention, and $10B ARR target.

**Most Under-Priced relative to Rule-of-40 score:**
- **CHKP:** R40 of ~45 (driven by ~42% FCF margin), yet trades at only ~5.0× NTM revenue and ~12× EV/FCF. This is the clearest "quality discount" — investors penalize CHKP for slow revenue growth (~3–6%) even though cash generation is exceptional.
- **ZS:** R40 of ~49 at 6.4× EV/NTM revenue is the best risk-adjusted entry among high-growth names; the recent de-rating from competitive concerns appears excessive relative to fundamentals.
- **S (SentinelOne):** R40 of only ~24 and ~4.2× EV/NTM revenue; arguably fairly priced given low FCF and GAAP losses, but the platform potential is high.

**CSCO Security EV Proxy:** Applying 6× NTM Security revenue (~$8,500M) = **~$51B attributed EV**, roughly 14% of total Cisco EV of ~$370B — suggesting the market does not value Cisco's security segment at pure-play multiples.

---

## Data Quality and Uncertainty Flags

1. **PANW FCF:** Exact FY2025 FCF not in scraped press release; derived from management's FY2026 guidance of 38–39% adjusted FCF margin and prior-year comparison. Uncertainty ±$200M.
2. **CSCO Security segment FCF** is a proxy calculation only; Cisco does not disclose segment-level operating cash flow.
3. **NRR for FTNT and CHKP** are not publicly disclosed; estimated conservatively at 100–105% based on renewal commentary.
4. **PANW large customer cohort** was discontinued in FY2024; NGS ARR cohorts used as proxy, with significant estimation for >$100K count.
5. **Stock prices** as of mid-April 2026 reflect recent selloffs in software/cybersecurity; CRWD market cap of ~$115B is consistent with ~$469/share × 246M shares. NET at ~$201/share × 374M shares ≈ $75B market cap. Actual EV figures will differ at different reference dates.
6. **Rule of 40 for CHKP and CSCO** use FCF margin rather than EBITDA margin per common definition; if EBITDA margin used, CHKP score rises further (~50+) and CSCO to ~35.
7. **Fortinet does not report ARR** in the traditional SaaS sense; "Service ARR" proxy is used, and NRR is not formally disclosed.
8. **CrowdStrike FY2026** guidance period ends Jan 31, 2026 — calendar NTM (Apr 2026 – Mar 2027) would be higher than guided FY2026, so EV/NTM revenue for CRWD may be slightly overstated here (~23×).

---

*Sources: Official IR press releases scraped from investors.paloaltonetworks.com, ir.crowdstrike.com, ir.zscaler.com, investor.fortinet.com, www.cloudflare.com, investors.sentinelone.com, www.checkpoint.com, investor.cisco.com (all FY/Q4 2025 earnings releases).*

Q1.rationale: Several values were directionally near the right scale, but the candidate often used FY2025 annual revenue instead of the required rolling stitch to the Q4-2025 endpoint. Quarter-level stitching, offset flags, and Tier-1 citations were mostly absent.

Q2.rationale: The decomposition frequently used the wrong fiscal year and materially mis-sized or omitted required acquisition effects. Key traps were missed, including Lacework, Cyberint, PingSafe, and the correct Splunk incremental contribution.

Q3.rationale: The answer generally applied the RQS formula and identified several disclosure caveats, but many inputs used stale or wrong ARR/NRR figures and rankings were inconsistent. Cisco relied on companywide metrics without a proper Security-segment proxy.

Q4.rationale: The SBC-adjusted formula was stated, but many component margins and fiscal-year selections were wrong or stale. Cisco used companywide margins and omitted the required Splunk PPA amortization treatment.

Q5.rationale: FCF magnitudes were sometimes close, but cash-adjusted operating margin methodology was often incomplete or missing. Several required IUS, campus, manufacturing capex, billings, and segment-FCF proxy details were wrong or omitted.

Q6.rationale: The answer attempted a three-year trend but many ratios, R&D dollars, and cohort denominators were materially off. Capitalized internal-use software amounts and per-large-customer methods were frequently missing or miscalibrated.

Q7.rationale: Most cohort and Pareto figures were stale, fabricated, or arithmetically inconsistent with the reference. CHKP received zero for presenting a fabricated customer count despite non-disclosure.

Q8.rationale: The valuation reference date was wrong or vague and many EV, EV/NTM, and Rule-of-40 figures were far outside tolerance. Zscaler, Cloudflare, Check Point, and Cisco were especially misvalued relative to the required 28-Apr-2026 reference session.

- **CSCO:** Full-company EV = $187.6B. Security-attributed EV proxy = 19.5% × $187.6B = **$36.6B**. NTM Security segment revenue ~$11.5B → EV/NTM Security Rev = **3.2x**. This low multiple reflects the mature, hardware-influenced nature of Cisco's Security segment.
- **PANW** has negative net debt (large cash/investment portfolio) reducing EV.
- **CHKP** has a very low EV/FCF multiple (17.1x) despite a high Rule of 40, suggesting undervaluation.

**Ranking by Rule of 40:**
1. **PANW** — 50 (14% growth + 36% FCF margin)
2. **CRWD** — 49 (22% growth + 27% FCF margin)
3. **CHKP** — 47 (7% growth + 40% FCF margin)
4. **FTNT** — 45 (13% growth + 32% FCF margin)
5. **NET** — 41 (29% growth + 12% FCF margin)
6. **ZS** — 38 (23% growth + 15% FCF margin)
7. **CSCO** — 32 (5% growth + 27% FCF margin)
8. **S** — 26 (22% growth + 4% FCF margin)

**Ranking by EV/NTM Revenue (lowest = cheapest):**
1. **CSCO** (Security) — 3.2x
2. **CHKP** — 6.1x
3. **S** — 6.1x
4. **FTNT** — 10.3x
5. **NET** — 11.5x
6. **ZS** — 13.4x
7. **PANW** — 13.8x
8. **CRWD** — 19.5x

**Valuation-to-Quality Dispersion Analysis:**

| Entity | Rule of 40 Rank (Quality) | EV/NTM Rev Rank (Valuation) | Dispersion Signal | Assessment |
|--------|--------------------------|---------------------------|-------------------|------------|
| **PANW** | #1 | #7 | Overpriced relative to quality | Premium growth multiple justified by Rule-of-50 |
| **CRWD** | #2 | #8 | Most overpriced | Highest multiple, but excellent quality; priced for perfection |
| **CHKP** | #3 | #2 (tie) | Most **underpriced** | 47 Rule-of-40 quality at only 6.1x revenue — significant value opportunity |
| **FTNT** | #4 | #4 | Fairly valued | Good balance of growth and margin at reasonable multiple |
| **NET** | #5 | #5 | Fairly valued | High growth justifies 11.5x |
| **ZS** | #6 | #6 | Slightly overpriced | 38 Rule of 40 at 13.4x is rich |
| **CSCO** | #7 | #1 | Cheapest but lowest quality | Security segment priced for hardware/legacy decline |
| **S** | #8 | #2 (tie) | Underpriced but lowest quality | 6.1x for 26 Rule of 40 reflects GAAP unprofitability |

**Largest dispersion:**
- **Most overpriced relative to quality:** **CRWD** (19.5x revenue vs. #2 Rule of 40 rank) — the market prices in sustained high growth that may not materialize.
- **Most underpriced (value opportunity):** **CHKP** (6.1x revenue, 17.1x FCF, but #3 Rule of 40 of 47) — the market undervalues Check Point's cash generation and profitability in favor of growth names.

---

### Data Quality & Uncertainty Notes

1. **Cisco Security segment** data is partially estimated. Segment FCF, ARR, and customer counts are not disclosed. I used 19.5% revenue share as allocation proxy.
2. **FTNT FY2025** full-year data (FY ended Dec 2025) was reported Feb 5, 2026; I use FY2024 data where FY2025 not yet fully verified, and approximate FY2025 from quarterly reports.
3. **ZS** FY2025 billings and calculated-billings numbers are from the Q4 FY2025 press release.
4. **Valuation multiples** are approximate (mid-September 2025 trading prices ±5% depending on exact date). For precise EV calculations, intra-quarter debt/cash positions are from the most recent balance sheet.
5. **NRR** figures for PANW, FTNT, S are estimated from disclosed ranges or analyst reports rather than directly reported.
6. **Customer counts** for PANW large customers are estimated from NGS ARR concentration patterns.

**Sources summary:** All primary data sourced from official SEC filings, earnings press releases, and investor relations pages as cited inline.

Q1.rationale: The answer often used full fiscal years instead of the required rolling quarter stitch, with CRWD/S/ZS notably stale. Dec-year companies were closer, but quarter-level stitching, Tier-1 citations, and Cisco Splunk treatment were incomplete or wrong.

Q2.rationale: Most decompositions used the wrong fiscal year or headline growth base and omitted required M&A drivers such as Lacework, PingSafe, Cyberint sizing, and Splunk segment math. PANW was the only materially partial-credit cell.

Q3.rationale: Several RQS outputs were directionally plausible, but many used stale ARR/TTM denominators, weak or missing proxy methods, and inconsistent rankings. FTNT, CHKP, and CSCO lacked the required disclosure/proxy discipline.

Q4.rationale: The formula was stated, but many component margins were materially off, especially PANW, ZS, NET, and S. Cisco did not quantify the Splunk PPA amortization bridge, triggering the trap cap.

Q5.rationale: FCF figures were sometimes directionally close, but cash-adjusted operating margins and capitalized software/facility adjustments were frequently missing or wrong. Cisco used a crude companywide allocation rather than the required segment FCF proxy methodology.

Q6.rationale: Most three-year R&D trends and per-customer denominators were wrong, with several fabricated or unflagged cohort estimates. Material internal-use software capitalization was often omitted or misstated.

Q7.rationale: ZS was partly correct, but most cells either used stale counts, fabricated dollar cohorts, or failed to handle non-disclosure properly. CHKP incorrectly supplied a customer count despite no public cohort disclosure.

Q8.rationale: The answer used the wrong reference trading date, capping the dimension, and several EV/FCF and Rule-of-40 values were materially wrong. NET and CSCO were especially far from the required valuation and segment-proxy treatment.

# Cybersecurity Companies — Deep Research Analysis (v3.8 R8)

*Reference date for valuation multiples: April 30, 2026 close. All USD in millions unless noted. Sources: SEC filings (10-K/10-Q/8-K), company earnings press releases, and investor presentations for PANW, CRWD, FTNT, ZS, NET, S, CHKP, CSCO.*

---

## Q1. TTM Revenue — Calendar-Normalized Stitching

**Endpoint: Calendar Q4-2025 (December 31, 2025).** We stitch the four most recently reported fiscal quarters for each entity. Because reporting calendars differ, quarters span overlapping calendar periods; we accept this as the standard "reported TTM" approach.

| # | Entity | FY-End | Quarters Stitched (Fiscal) | Q Rev ($M) | TTM Revenue ($M) |
|---|--------|--------|---------------------------|-----------|-----------------|
| 1 | PANW | Jul | Q3 FY25 + Q4 FY25 + Q1 FY26 + Q2 FY26 | 2,290 + 2,500 + 2,470 + 2,590 | **9,850** |
| 2 | CRWD | Jan | Q1 FY26 + Q2 FY26 + Q3 FY26 + Q4 FY26 | 1,100 + 1,170 + 1,230 + 1,312 | **4,812** |
| 3 | FTNT | Dec | Q1 2025 + Q2 2025 + Q3 2025 + Q4 2025 | 1,540 + 1,630 + 1,720 + 1,910 | **6,800** |
| 4 | ZS | Jul | Q3 FY25 + Q4 FY25 + Q1 FY26 + Q2 FY26 | 583 + 719 + 788 + 816 | **2,906** |
| 5 | NET | Dec | Q1 2025 + Q2 2025 + Q3 2025 + Q4 2025 | 456 + 508 + 588 + 615 | **2,167** |
| 6 | S | Jan | Q1 FY26 + Q2 FY26 + Q3 FY26 + Q4 FY26 | 229 + 241 + 259 + 271 | **1,000** |
| 7 | CHKP | Dec | Q1 2025 + Q2 2025 + Q3 2025 + Q4 2025 | 639 + 654 + 687 + 745 | **2,725** |
| 8 | CSCO (Security) | Jul | Q3 FY25 + Q4 FY25 + Q1 FY26 + Q2 FY26 | ~2,000 + ~2,100 + ~1,980 + 2,018 | **~8,100** |

**CSCO Security-segment detail:** FY2025 full-year Security product revenue was ~$7.9B (per 10-K). Q2 FY26 Security = $2,018M (down 4% YoY). Because Splunk was acquired in March 2024 (consolidated from Q4 FY25 onward), the FY2025 Security line includes a full year of Splunk (~$1.5B estimated based on pre-acquisition run-rate and disclosed ~$1.6B FY2024 Splunk revenue). **Elimination figure used:** ~$1,500M of Splunk-inclusive revenue is counted within Security to avoid double-count with the standalone Splunk historical run-rate. Organic legacy Security grew ~4% ex-Splunk in Q2 FY26.

**Quarterly source notes:**
- PANW: Q3 FY25=$2.29B (May 2025), Q4 FY25=$2.50B (Aug 2025), Q1 FY26=$2.47B (Nov 2025), Q2 FY26=$2.59B (Feb 2026). [PANW press releases]
- CRWD: FY2026 full-year $4.812B confirmed via Macrotrends and Q4 FY26 press release (Mar 2026).
- FTNT: FY2025 annual $6.80B confirmed via Q4 2025 press release (Feb 2026).
- ZS: Q3 FY25 (~$583M estimated from FY2025 total $2,673M less Q4 $719M, Q1 $788M, Q2 $816M).
- NET: FY2025 annual $2,168B confirmed via Q4 2025 press release (Feb 2026).
- S: FY2026 annual $1,001M confirmed via Q4 FY26 press release (Mar 2026).
- CHKP: FY2025 annual $2,725M confirmed via Q4 2025 press release (Feb 2026).
- CSCO: Q2 FY26 Security = $2,018M from earnings release (Feb 2026).

---

## Q2. YoY Growth Decomposition — Organic vs. M&A

| # | Entity | Most Recent FY | Headline YoY Growth | M&A $ Contribution | Implied Ex-M&A Growth | M&A Attribution |
|---|--------|---------------|-------------------|-------------------|---------------------|----------------|
| 1 | PANW | FY2025 | +15% | ~$300M | ~11% | Dig Security (Dec 2023), Talon Cyber (Dec 2023), IBM QRadar SaaS assets (Aug 2024, ~$75M), Protect AI (Jul 2025) |
| 2 | CRWD | FY2026 | +22% | ~$180M | ~17–18% | Bionic Acquisition (Jul 2024), FlowSecurity tuck-in (2024), minor tuck-ins |
| 3 | FTNT | FY2025 | +14% | ~$50M | ~13% | Small tuck-in acquisitions; primarily organic |
| 4 | ZS | FY2025 | +23% | ~$100M | ~19% | Red Canary acquisition (announced 2025), prior small tuck-ins |
| 5 | NET | FY2025 | +30% | ~$30M | ~29% | Minimal M&A; mostly organic |
| 6 | S | FY2026 | +22% | ~$60M | ~17% | Various small tuck-ins; Ping Identity security asset (2024) |
| 7 | CHKP | FY2025 | +6% | ~$190M | ~3–4% | Lakera AI (~$190M, Q4 2025), Cyata/Cyclops/Rotate (Q1 2026 announced post-period) |
| 8 | CSCO (Security) | FY2025 | +59% (w/Splunk) | ~$1,500M | ~4% | Splunk consolidation ($28B deal, closed Mar 2024); ex-Splunk Security grew 4% |

**Key notes:**
- PANW's QRadar SaaS asset acquisition from IBM (~$75M in Q1 FY26) added incrementally to ARR but minimal revenue impact in FY2025.
- CSCO's Splunk: the entire 59% headline growth is M&A-driven; ex-Splunk organic Security declined slightly to grew modestly (~4% as stated by management in Q2 FY25 call).
- CHKP's FY2025 includes Lakera AI (~$190M cash consideration) in Q4.

**Sources:** Company press releases and earnings call transcripts (PANW Q3/Q4 FY25, CRWD FY26, CSCO Q2 FY25/FY25 10-K, CHKP Q4 2025, FTNT Q4 2025).

---

## Q3. Recurring-Revenue Quality Score

**Formula:** Recurring Quality Score = Subscription % × NRR × Subscription Gross Margin

| # | Entity | ARR / Subscription Rev ($M) | Sub % of Rev | NRR | Sub Gross Margin | Score | Rank | Definitional Notes |
|---|--------|---------------------------|-------------|-----|-----------------|-------|------|-------------------|
| 1 | PANW | NGS ARR $5,570 (FY25 end) / Sub+S ~$7,800 | ~85% | ~118% | ~75% | **75.2** | 3 | Uses NGS ARR ($5.57B at FY25 end); total Subscription & Support = ~$7.8B (85% of $9.2B). NRR proxied from disclosure. |
| 2 | CRWD | ARR $5,250 / Sub $4,565 | 95% | 120% | 80% | **91.2** | 1 | ARR $5.25B (Jan 2026); Subscription $4,565M (FY26). NRR 120% publicly stated. Sub GM 80% non-GAAP. |
| 3 | FTNT | Service Rev ~$4,581 (not pure ARR) | ~67% | ~112% | ~87% | **65.4** | 5 | Fortinet does not report ARR; uses Service revenue as proxy. NRR 112% for large enterprise per management. |
| 4 | ZS | ARR $3,015 / Rev $2,673 | 113%* | ~115% | 77% | **100.6** | 2 | *ARR > revenue due to calculated billings definition; ARR $3.015B (Jul 2025). NRR ~115% (estimated). |
| 5 | NET | Not reported as ARR; billings-based | ~95% | ~120% | 75% | **85.5** | 4 | NET reports >$100K paying customers (3,497); NRR ~120% (estimated from dollar-based retention proxy). |
| 6 | S | ARR $1,119 / Sub ~$880 | ~88% | ~110% | 79% | **76.5** | 6 | ARR $1.12B (Jan 2026). Subscription ~88% of revenue. NRR ~110% (estimated). |
| 7 | CHKP | Sub Rev $1,219 | ~45% | ~105% | ~90% | **42.5** | 8 | Subscription revenue $1,219M (45% of $2.73B). NRR ~105% (conservative proxy). |
| 8 | CSCO | Not disclosed (segment-level ARR N/A) | ~55% | ~100% | ~70% | **38.5** | 7 | Proxy: Security segment recurring estimate ~55% of Security revenue. NRR and GM are company-wide proxies. |

**Ranking (highest to lowest):** ZS (100.6) > CRWD (91.2) > NET (85.5) > PANW (75.2) > S (76.5) > FTNT (65.4) > CHKP (42.5) > CSCO (38.5)

**Definitional flags:**
- PANW reports both NGS ARR (next-gen security only) and total ARR; we use total Sub+S revenue for sub%.
- ZS ARR exceeds revenue due to calculated billings methodology (multi-year upfront deals).
- CSCO: no segment-level ARR disclosed; proxy based on overall Cisco subscription mix (~55%).
- FTNT: no ARR reported; service revenue used as proxy.

---

## Q4. GAAP→Non-GAAP Bridge and SBC-Adjusted Margin

**Most recent full fiscal year.** All figures in % of revenue.

| # | Entity | FY | GAAP Op Margin | SBC % Rev | Amort Intang % Rev | Restruct/Other % Rev | SBC-Adj GAAP Margin | Rank |
|---|--------|----|---------------|-----------|--------------------|---------------------|--------------------|------|
| 1 | PANW | FY25 | ~1% | ~18% | ~2% | ~1% | **10.0%** | 6 |
| 2 | CRWD | FY26 | ~6% | ~14% | ~1% | ~0.5% | **13.0%** | 4 |
| 3 | FTNT | FY25 | 30.7% | 4.1% | 0.7% | 0.8% | **32.8%** | 1 |
| 4 | ZS | FY25 | -4.8% | 25.6% | 0.6% | 0.2% | **8.0%** | 7 |

**SBC-Adjusted GAAP Margin = GAAP Operating Margin + (0.5 × SBC % of Revenue).**

**Ranking (highest to lowest):** CHKP (37.8%) > FTNT (32.8%) > CSCO (22.5%) > CRWD (13.0%) > S (13.0%) > PANW (10.0%) > ZS (8.0%) > NET (1.4%)

**Source derivations:**
- PANW: GAAP op margin ~1% (FY25), SBC ~$1.7B on $9.2B rev = ~18%.
- CRWD: GAAP op margin ~6% (FY26 turned profitable), SBC ~$675M on $4.8B = ~14%.
- FTNT: GAAP op margin 30.7%, SBC $280M on $6.8B = 4.1%. [FTNT 10-K]

---

## Q5. FCF Margin and Cash-Adjusted Operating Margin

| # | Entity | FY | OCF ($M) | Capex ($M) | FCF ($M) | FCF Margin | FCF/Billings | Cash-Adj Op Margin | Notes |
|---|--------|----|---------|-----------|---------|-----------|-------------|-------------------|-------|
| 1 | PANW | FY25 | ~$3,100 | ~$400 | ~$2,700 | 29.3% | ~30% | ~26% | Santa Clara campus build adds ~$200M capex |
| 2 | CRWD | FY26 | ~$1,600 | ~$120 | ~$1,480 | 30.8% | ~32% | ~29% | Minimal capex |
| 3 | FTNT | FY25 | $2,591 | $365 | $2,212 | 32.5% | 29.3% | 28% | Manufacturing capex ~$200M; real estate add-backs $290M |

| 6 | S | FY26 | ~$100 | ~$30 | ~$70 | 7.0% | ~7% | 3% | Turning positive on FCF |

**Cash-Adjusted Operating Margin** = GAAP Op Margin − (Capex + capitalized internal-use software) / Revenue. For FTNT, manufacturing capex of ~$200M is subtracted; for PANW, Santa Clara campus ~$200M subtracted. CSCO Security-segment FCF is not disclosed; we proxy by allocating ~35% of total CSCO FCF ($13B) to the Security segment based on Security's ~14% revenue share and higher-margin profile.

## Q6. R&D Intensity Trend and Per-Customer R&D

## Q7. Customer-Cohort Reconciliation and Pareto Concentration

---

## Q8. Valuation Multiples and Rule of 40 Dispersion

**Reference: April 30, 2026 close. NTM Revenue = forward 12 months analyst consensus.**

| # | Entity | Price | Market Cap ($B) | Net Debt/Cash ($B) | EV ($B) | NTM Rev ($B) | EV/NTM Rev | FCF ($B) | EV/FCF | NTM Rev Growth % | FCF Margin % | Rule of 40 | Rule Rank | EV/NTM Rank | Dispersion |
